newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordanian stocks steady in some foreign buying.
newsitem.headline: Jordanian stocks steady in some foreign buying.

text.p: Jordanian shares fell slightly on Monday but were buttressed by some foreign-inspired buying orders in select blue-chip shares, dealers said.
The official 60-share Amman Financial Market (AFM) index fell 0.19 percent to 164.47 points after turnover worth 766,611 dinars ($1.1 million).
Investor interest was focused on Jordan Cement Factories which posted a 0.04 dinar gain to four dinars in busy trade worth 100,439 dinars.
Another popular stock with emerging funds, Jordan Phosphate Mines, which has floated a $100 million eurobond, rose 0.05 dinars, also to four dinars.
"The activity was normal and focused on some stock in certain positions in which some foreign buying was detected," said broker Husam al-Hanbali.
Heavyweight Arab Bank, which drove the official index up to a three-year high earlier in July, lost 1.50 dinars to 287.50 dinars in poor trade of just 440 shares.
Local investors piled into the shares in recent weeks, anticipating strong 1997 profits, announcements of a bonus share offering and government plans to scrap foreign share ownership ceilings.
But cancellation of the 50 percent foreign ownership ceiling has been delayed in cabinet, deflating the Arab Bank bubble.
Overall five shares rose on Monday and 18 fell with another 19 trading but closing unchanged.

The private Pearl Index of the 45 best-performing shares in terms of turnover and financial performance, fixed at 100 points at the end of 1994, fell 0.25 percent to 80.46 points, 3.51 percent down since the start of the year. $1 = 0.709 dinars
